title: Quorum — Distributed Systems Lab
description: A deterministic distributed-systems simulator: Raft, Multi-Paxos, Viewstamped Replication (the third canonical crash-fault consensus protocol — a deterministic primary at view mod N drives Prepare/PrepareOk/Commit, backups run StartViewChange→DoViewChange→StartView to rotate the primary and rebuild the log from a quorum, and a crashed replica runs an explicit recovery protocol to rebuild its state from its peers, all with no stable storage), Zab — the ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast protocol (the fourth canonical crash-fault protocol and the one deployed at scale, built for the primary-backup pattern: an elected primary stamps every write with a zxid = (epoch, counter) and atomically broadcasts it so replicas deliver in the exact order the primary issued — Zab's primary-order guarantee — running all four phases from the DSN 2011 paper: Fast Leader Election picks the peer with the most up-to-date log, Discovery settles a new epoch, Synchronization forces the newest history onto a quorum so everyone starts identical, and Broadcast is normal two-phase Propose/Ack/Commit; unlike VR it keeps a DURABLE log so a restarted node recovers by reconciliation not replay, with five safety invariants — Agreement/total-order, Primary Order, Leader Uniqueness, Execution Safety, Log Well-Formed — held green through a 150-seed chaos sweep that surfaced and fixed a learner over-delivery bug, an FLE livelock on a dead ex-leader, and a split-brain election deadlock) and leaderless EPaxos consensus (egalitarian, dependency-graph ordering with fast/slow paths, SCC execution and explicit-prepare recovery), Ben-Or randomized consensus (the protocol that defeats the FLP impossibility with coin flips — no leader, no stable storage, no synchrony: Report/Propose rounds where a strict majority forms a proposal, f+1 matching proposals decide, and an inconclusive round is broken by a coin toss; safety is deterministic and unconditional while termination is probabilistic-with-probability-1), PBFT and HotStuff Byzantine fault tolerance (survive malicious replicas), Snow/Avalanche metastable consensus (Slush/Snowflake/Snowball — agreement by random subsampling instead of quorums, with a live opinion-over-time chart and Byzantine resilience), a Dynamo-style tunable-quorum store (sloppy quorums, hinted handoff, read repair, vector-clock siblings), a Chord DHT, CRDTs, gossip/SWIM failure detection, vector clocks and 2PC/3PC, an ABD linearizable register (atomic read/write storage with no consensus), CRAQ chain replication (linearizable storage by topology not quorums — a HEAD→…→TAIL chain where writes commit at the tail and every replica serves reads, with a master, config leases, a chain-currency heartbeat and lease-based reconfiguration keeping reads linearizable through crashes, master loss and partitions, cross-checked by the general checker), Chandy–Lamport consistent global snapshots (FIFO-channel marker algorithm recording a consistent cut of a running, conserved token economy), Lamport logical-clock mutual exclusion (REQUEST/REPLY/RELEASE ordered by (timestamp,id) — distributed locking with no lock server), Bracha Byzantine reliable broadcast (SEND/ECHO/READY amplification surviving an equivocating sender at N≥3f+1), and a from-scratch Wing & Gong linearizability checker (the NP-complete decision procedure, made tractable by real-time pruning, memoized dead ends and Herlihy–Wing locality) that works for any sequential object — register/CAS/counter/set/FIFO-queue/stack/lock — certifying a passing history with a concrete witness order and convicting a failing one by naming the operation that went back in time, run on textbook counterexamples, random schedules and real ABD runs harvested live off the kernel; all from scratch on one seeded discrete-event kernel with a controllable network, time-travel scrubbing and live invariant checking.
